description: Each state's matched count is divided by the sum of the matched counts across all states.

c.request: Counting `player_college` records under the `state` of their college (matching on exactly equal `college_id`; records whose college isn't found don't count toward any state; a blank or missing state is its own group), how many records does each state have, and what share of the player-college records is that? Don't round. Each state's matched count is divided by the sum of the matched counts across all states.
c.sql: SELECT c.state AS state, COUNT(*) AS record_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY c.state

b.request: For each state of the college (joining `player_college` to `college` on equal `college_id`, excluding records with no matching college, and treating a blank or missing state as its own group), report the number of matched records and that count divided by the total number of matched records across all states, unrounded
b.sql: SELECT COALESCE(c.state, '') AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS proportion FROM player_college pc INNER JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY COALESCE(c.state, '')

a.request: Match each `player_college` record to `college` on exactly equal `college_id`, and leave out records whose college isn't found. For each college `state` (a blank or missing state is its own group), give the state, its number of matched records, and that number divided by the sum of the matched counts over all states, so the shares add up to 1. Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT c.state AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY c.state

d.request: Counting `player_college` records under the `state` of their college (matching on exactly equal `college_id`; records whose college isn't found don't count toward any state; a blank or missing state is its own group), how many records does each state have, and what share is that, where each state's share is its matched count divided by the sum of the matched counts across all states (so records with no matching college are excluded from the denominator)? Don't round.
d.sql: SELECT c.state AS state, COUNT(*) AS record_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY c.state
